appraisal_events.evidence: Ma mère, pleine de respect pour les occupations de mon père, vint demander, timidement, si elle pouvait faire servir. Elle avait peur d'interrompre une conversation où elle n'aurait pas eu à être mêlée.
appraisal_events.explanation: The mother approaches her own dining room timidly, marked as an outsider to the shared professional world of her husband and Norpois, which she fears to interrupt.

appraisal_events.evidence: la parfaite indépendance des muscles du visage à laquelle M. de Norpois était arrivé lui permettait d'écouter sans avoir l'air d'entendre; ... du visage de l'aristocratique virtuose ... sortait ... la phrase commencée, comme le piano ... réplique ... au violoncelle, dans un concerto de Mozart. Mon père finissait par se troubler.
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois's total command of the conversation's rhythm, rendered through an admiring musical metaphor, leaves the father visibly unsettled while waiting on his response.

status_effects.explanation: She remains at the edge of the collegial, professional exchange between her husband and Norpois, approaching only timidly and fearing to intrude.
Norpois's impassive, perfectly controlled pacing of the conversation is framed as virtuoso mastery, giving him complete command of the exchange.
The father grows visibly flustered waiting on Norpois's unreadable, delayed response, losing his own composure in the exchange.

ambiguities: The narrator's confession to Norpois that he was disappointed by la Berma is the passage's final beat, but Norpois's reaction to it is not shown here, so no status effect is recorded for that exchange in this unit.
